questions.q: India's first interplanetary mission is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission).

Key Points

• Mangalyaan, also known as the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), was launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on 5 November 2013.
• This mission made India the first Asian nation to reach Martian orbit and the fourth space agency globally to do so after NASA, the Soviet space program, and the European Space Agency.
• The spacecraft was launched aboard the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-C25) from the Sriharikota spaceport.
• Mangalyaan was designed to study the Martian surface, morphology, atmosphere, and mineralogy, contributing significantly to Mars exploration.
• The mission was executed with a remarkably low budget of approximately ₹450 crores, making it one of the most cost-effective interplanetary missions globally.
• This achievement demonstrated India’s technological capabilities in deep space exploration and inspired future missions like Chandrayaan-2 and Aditya-L1.
Additional Information

• Chandrayaan-1:
• Chandrayaan-1 was India’s first lunar probe, launched on 22 October 2008.
• It discovered the presence of water molecules on the Moon’s surface, a landmark finding in space science.
• The mission was instrumental in mapping the Moon’s surface composition and topography.
• The spacecraft carried 11 payloads, including instruments from ISRO, NASA, ESA, and other international agencies.
• Gaganyaan:
• The Gaganyaan mission is India’s first human spaceflight program scheduled for launch by 2024.
• The mission aims to send Indian astronauts, known as Vyomanauts, to low Earth orbit aboard an Indian-made spacecraft.
• It includes orbital crew modules developed by ISRO and emphasizes human space exploration capabilities.
• Aditya-L1:
• Aditya-L1 is India’s first solar mission, launched by ISRO to study the Sun’s corona, solar emissions, and solar wind.
• The spacecraft will be placed in a Lagrangian point (L1) between the Earth and the Sun for continuous observation.
• This mission will provide valuable insights into space weather phenomena and their impact on Earth.
• India’s Space Achievements:
• India is among the leading countries in space exploration, with missions like Chandrayaan-2, RISAT, and GSAT satellites.
• ISRO’s focus on cost-effective technology has garnered global recognition, including its commercial satellite launches via the PSLV.
Important Points

• ISRO’s Role:
• ISRO has been pivotal in advancing India’s space capabilities, with missions like Mangalyaan, Chandrayaan, and Gaganyaan.
• Its achievements demonstrate self-reliance in satellite technology and interplanetary exploration.
• International Collaboration:
• ISRO has collaborated with agencies like NASA, ESA, and Roscosmos for research and payload development.
• Such partnerships enhance India’s scientific and technological expertise in space exploration.
• Budget and Efficiency:
• ISRO’s missions are known for their cost-effectiveness, making it a preferred option for commercial satellite launches.
• Mangalyaan’s budget of ₹450 crores showcases India’s capability for efficient space mission execution.

questions.q: Under which Act was a Law Commission first established in India to codify and consolidate Indian laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Charter Act, 1833.

Key Points

• The Charter Act, 1833 was a landmark legislation passed by the British Parliament, marking significant changes in the administration of India.

• It was the first act that provided for the establishment of a Law Commission in India with the purpose of codifying and consolidating Indian laws.

• The Law Commission was headed by Lord Macaulay, who played a major role in drafting the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and introducing English as the medium of legal and administrative education.

• The Act centralized legislative authority in India by vesting all law-making powers with the Governor-General of India in Council, aiming to unify laws across British-controlled territories.

• The main objective of the Law Commission was to ensure a uniform system of laws for India, which would replace diverse systems of customary laws and local practices.

Additional Information

• Charter Act, 1833:

• The Act abolished the trading rights of the East India Company, transforming it into a purely administrative body.

• It introduced civil services examinations to recruit officials in British India, laying the foundation for modern bureaucracy.

• Under this Act, Lord William Bentinck was appointed as the first Governor-General of India, unifying the administration of Bengal, Madras, and Bombay under one authority.

• The Act aimed to promote the idea of legal uniformity, eventually influencing the codification of Indian laws like the IPC and CPC.

• Law Commission of India:

• The first Law Commission was established in 1834 under the Charter Act, 1833, with Lord Macaulay as its chairman.

• It played a pivotal role in drafting laws that still exist in modern Indian legal systems, such as the Indian Penal Code (1860), the Code of Civil Procedure (1859), and the Criminal Procedure Code (1861).

• Indian Penal Code (IPC):

• The IPC was drafted by the first Law Commission and came into force in 1860.

• It is the primary criminal code in India, providing detailed provisions for crimes, punishments, and procedural safeguards.

• The code is structured into 23 chapters and 511 sections, covering offenses ranging from theft to murder and cybercrimes.

• Other Relevant Legislative Acts:

• Regulating Act, 1773: Introduced the first attempt at regulating the East India Company's affairs but did not include provisions for law codification.

• Government of India Act, 1858: Transferred administrative control from the East India Company to the British Crown but was not responsible for establishing the Law Commission.

• Indian Councils Act, 1861: Marked the beginning of legislative councils but had no role in codifying laws.

Important Points

• Impact of the Charter Act, 1833:

• The Act centralized legislative powers and paved the way for a unified legal system in India.

• It laid the foundation for modern legal and bureaucratic systems that continue to influence Indian governance.

• Lord Macaulay's Contribution:

• As chairman of the Law Commission, Lord Macaulay was instrumental in drafting the IPC and shaping modern Indian law.

• He advocated the use of English for legal and administrative purposes, fostering a uniform system of governance.

questions.q: Which of the following is usually excluded when measuring a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?
options: Consumer spending on final goods and services.
The value of intermediate goods used in production.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The value of intermediate goods used in production..

Key Points

• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a specific time period.
• The value of intermediate goods is excluded from GDP calculations to avoid double counting, which would otherwise inflate GDP figures.
• Intermediate goods are those used as inputs in the production of other goods and services, such as raw materials or components.
• Only the value of final goods and services, which are sold to the end-user, is included in GDP measurements.
• For instance, if a car manufacturer buys steel to produce a car, the value of steel is not separately added to GDP, as it is already accounted for in the final price of the car.
Additional Information

• Components of GDP:
• Consumer Spending: Includes household expenditures on goods and services like food, clothing, and entertainment.
• Government Expenditure: Includes government spending on public services such as education, defense, and infrastructure.
• Net Exports: Calculated as exports minus imports. A positive net export contributes to GDP, while a negative net export reduces it.
• Why Intermediate Goods Are Excluded:
• Including intermediate goods in GDP would lead to double counting, as their value is already embedded in the final goods.
• This exclusion ensures an accurate and undistorted representation of a country's economic output.
• Examples of Intermediate and Final Goods:
• Intermediate Goods: Steel used in construction, flour used by bakeries to make bread.
• Final Goods: Cars sold to consumers, bread sold at grocery stores.
• Methods of GDP Calculation:
• Production Approach: Calculates GDP based on the value added at each stage of production.
• Income Approach: Summarizes all incomes earned in the economy, such as wages, rents, and profits.
• Expenditure Approach: Totals all expenditures on final goods and services.
Important Points

• Consumer Spending: Largest component of GDP in many economies, reflecting the purchasing power and demand of households.
• Government Expenditure: Includes spending on infrastructure projects and public services, crucial for economic development.
• Net Exports: A key indicator of a country's trade balance, influencing its economic health and GDP.
• Intermediate Goods in Context: Their exclusion highlights the importance of focusing on value addition in GDP metrics.
• Relevance of GDP: Used as an indicator of economic performance and to compare economic activity across nations.

questions.q: Which of the following numbers has a terminating decimal representation?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

A fraction in its lowest terms represents a terminating decimal if its denominator has only 2 and/or 5 as prime factors.

Checking the options:

Denominator of 3/8 is 8, and its prime factorization is 8 = 2³.

Since the only prime factor is 2, the fraction 3/8 will have a terminating decimal representation.

∴ The correct answer is 3/8.

Alternate Method

Given:

Fractions provided in the options: 3/8, 1/6, 2/7, 4/9

Method Used:

We can manually divide the numerator by the denominator to observe the decimal sequence.

Calculations:

⇒ 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 (This stops after three decimal places, meaning it terminates)

⇒ 1 ÷ 6 = 0.16666... (The digit 6 repeats endlessly)

⇒ 2 ÷ 7 = 0.285714285714... (The sequence 285714 repeats endlessly)

⇒ 4 ÷ 9 = 0.44444... (The digit 4 repeats endlessly)

⇒ Out of all options, only 3/8 gives a finite and exact decimal output.

∴ The correct answer is 3/8.

Additional Information

Terminating Decimal

A decimal number that contains a finite number of digits after the decimal point. This happens precisely when the fraction's denominator (in simplest form) is of the form 2m × 5ⁿ, where m and n are non-negative integers.

Non-Terminating Repeating Decimal

A decimal that continues endlessly but features a repeating pattern of digits (e.g., 1/3 = 0.333...). This happens when the denominator has prime factors other than 2 or 5 (like 3, 7, 11, etc.).

Irrational Numbers

Numbers that have non-terminating and non-repeating decimal expansions (e.g., √2, √3, π). These cannot be expressed as a simple fraction of two integers.

questions.q: Ajay and Vijay start from the same point and walk at 4 km/h and 5 km/h respectively, in the same direction. What will be the distance between them after 2 hours?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 5 − 4 = 1 km/h.

Distance gap after 2 hours = Relative speed × Time = 1 × 2 = 2 km.

∴ The correct answer is 2 km.

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Distance covered by Vijay in 2 hours = 5 × 2 = 10 km

⇒ Since they are walking in the same direction, the distance between them is the difference of distances covered.

⇒ Distance between them = 10 − 8 = 2 km

∴ The correct answer is 2 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated as the difference between their individual speeds. Relative speed = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds. Relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Distance Formula

Distance is defined as the product of speed and time. The formula used is D = S × T, maintaining corresponding units like km/h and hours.

questions.q: A spherical balloon is inflated, causing its radius to grow by 10%. By what percentage does its surface area increase?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The surface area of a sphere is proportional to the square of its radius (r²).

When a dimension increases by x%, the percentage increase in area is found using the successive percentage formula: x + x + (x × x) ÷ 100

Given the increase in radius, x = 10%

Percentage increase in surface area = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 20 + 1 = 21%

∴ The correct answer is 21%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Increase in the radius of the spherical balloon = 10%

Formula Used:

Surface Area of a sphere = 4πr²

• r Initial Area = 4πr²
• 1.1r New Area = 1.21 × 4πr²
•
+10% Radius Surface Area Increase = 21%

Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial radius of the sphere be r.

⇒ Initial Surface Area (A₁) = 4πr²

⇒ New radius after 10% increase = r + (10 ÷ 100)r = 1.1r

⇒ New Surface Area (A₂) = 4π(1.1r)²

⇒ A₂ = 4π(1.21r²) = 1.21(4πr²)

⇒ Increase in Area = A₂ − A₁ = 1.21(4πr²) − 1(4πr²) = 0.21(4πr²)

⇒ Percentage increase = (Increase in Area ÷ Initial Area) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = [0.21(4πr²) ÷ 4πr²] × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 0.21 × 100 = 21%

∴ The correct answer is 21%.

Additional Information

Volume Percentage Change

Since the volume of a sphere depends on the cube of its radius (r³), the percentage change in volume is calculated by applying the percentage change successively three times, or by evaluating [(1 + x/100)³ − 1] × 100.

Successive Percentage Formula

For two consecutive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%. This is particularly useful for 2D mensuration problems involving area.

1D Dimension Change

Any one-dimensional measurement like circumference, diameter, or perimeter changes by the exact same percentage as the radius. Therefore, a 10% increase in radius will yield exactly a 10% increase in the circumference.

Volume Conversions

1 m³ = 1000 liters, and 1 liter = 1000 cm³. These standard unit conversions are critical for solving 3D mensuration and capacity problems effectively.

Capacity vs Volume

Volume measures the amount of 3-dimensional space occupied by an object, while capacity refers to the amount of liquid a hollow container can hold. Capacity is generally measured in liters (L) or milliliters (mL).

Fraction Shortcut for Decimals

Converting decimals to fractions often speeds up arithmetic division operations. For example, knowing that 0.25 is 1/4 means 6.25 can be written as 25/4. Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.

questions.q: The area of a regular triangle increases by 44%. By what percentage did the side length increase?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For any 2D geometrical figure, Area ∝ (Side)².

Since the area increases by 44%, the new area becomes 144% of the original, which corresponds to a multiplying factor of 1.44.

The multiplying factor for the side length will be the square root of the area factor: √1.44 = 1.2.

A multiplier of 1.2 means the side length has increased by 0.2, which is exactly 20%.

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

The area of a regular (equilateral) triangle increases by 44%.

Formula Used:

Area of an equilateral triangle = √3 ÷ 4 × a², where a is the side length.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial side length of the triangle be a.

⇒ Initial Area (A₁) = √3 ÷ 4 × a²

⇒ Final Area (A₂) = A₁ + 44% of A₁ = 1.44 × A₁

⇒ Let the final side length of the triangle be a'.

⇒ √3 ÷ 4 × (a')² = 1.44 × (√3 ÷ 4 × a²)

⇒ By cancelling out the common terms (√3 ÷ 4) on both sides:

⇒ (a')² = 1.44 × a²

⇒ Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ a' = 1.2 × a

⇒ Increase in side length = a' − a = 1.2a − a = 0.2a

⇒ Percentage increase in side length = (0.2a ÷ a) × 100 = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a 2D figure has its dimensions increased uniformly by x%, the total percentage change in its area is given by the formula: Area % Change = x + x + (x² ÷ 100). For x = 20%, Area Change = 20 + 20 + 400÷100 = 44%.

Area of Similar Figures

The ratio of the areas of any two similar regular geometric figures is directly proportional to the square of the ratio of their corresponding side lengths.

Properties of a Regular Triangle

A regular triangle is an equilateral triangle where all three sides are equal, all interior angles are 60°, and its height is determined by the formula: h = √3 ÷ 2 × side.

questions.solution:

Marked Price & Discount

questions.q: The average salary of 40 workers in a factory is Rs. 24,000. If the salary of a supervisor is added, the average rises to Rs. 24,500. What is the supervisor's salary?

⇒ Increase in average = 24500 − 24000 = Rs. 500

⇒ Supervisor's Salary = 24000 + (41 × 500) = Rs. 44,500

⇒ Total number of people including supervisor = 40 + 1 = 41

1. Replacement Method in Averages

When a new person replaces an old person: New Person's Value = Old Person's Value ± (Total Entities × Change in Average).

2. Combined (Weighted) Average

If group A has n₁ items with average A₁, and group B has n₂ items with average A₂, then Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

3. Shift in Origin and Scale

If every observation is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant value 'k', the new average also changes by applying the exact same arithmetic operation with 'k' on the old average.

questions.q: Two right prisms have the same height of 10 cm. One has a regular hexagonal base with side 6 cm, and the other has a square base with side 6 cm. What is the ratio of their volumes?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two right prisms have the same height, the ratio of their volumes is strictly equal to the ratio of their base areas.

Ratio = Area of regular hexagonal base : Area of square base

Ratio = [6 × (√3 / 4) × a²] : a²

Since the side length a = 6 cm is identical for both, a² cancels out completely.

Ratio = (3√3 / 2) : 1 = 3√3 : 2

∴ The correct answer is 3√3 : 2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of the square base (b) = 6 cm

Height of both right prisms (h) = 10 cm

Formula Used:

Area of a regular hexagon = (3√3 / 2) × (side)²

Area of a square = (side)²

Hexagonal Base a = 6 cm Square Base b = 6 cm Ratio of Volumes = Ratio of Base Areas

Calculation:

⇒ Volume of the hexagonal prism (V₁) = [(3√3 / 2) × 6²] × 10

⇒ V₁ = (3√3 / 2) × 36 × 10

⇒ V₁ = 54√3 × 10 = 540√3 cm³

⇒ Volume of the square prism (V₂) = [6²] × 10

⇒ V₂ = 36 × 10 = 360 cm³

⇒ Ratio of their volumes = V₁ : V₂

⇒ Ratio = 540√3 : 360

⇒ Dividing both sides by 180, we get:

⇒ Ratio = 3√3 : 2

∴ The correct answer is 3√3 : 2.

Additional Information

Volume of a Prism

The volume of any right prism is calculated by multiplying its base area by its height. Formula: V = Base Area × height.

Total Surface Area of a Prism

The total surface area encompasses all the faces of the 3D shape. Formula: TSA = Lateral Surface Area + 2 × Base Area, where Lateral Surface Area = Base Perimeter × height.

Area of a Regular Hexagon

A regular hexagon behaves exactly like 6 adjacent equilateral triangles joined at the center. Area = 6 × (√3 / 4) × side² = (3√3 / 2) × side².

questions.q: A 45-litre mixture of kerosene and diesel contains kerosene and diesel in the ratio 4:5. How much diesel must be added to make the ratio 4:6?

Increase in Diesel parts = 6 − 5 = 1 part.

Constant Component Strategy

When one component is added or removed, the quantity of the other component remains unchanged. Equating its ratio parts directly yields the change in the total mixture.

Rule of Alligation

Used to find the ratio in which two ingredients are combined: Ratio = (Quantity of Cheaper) / (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) / (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper).

Replacement in Mixture

When a part of a mixture is replaced by one of its pure components, the ratio of ingredients in the remaining mixture initially remains the same as the original mixture.
